summary: 11 countries. No single American story owns the day. Foreign editors spread their attention across the $40 trillion debt milestone, a Chinese hacking network broken up by US agencies, courts pushing back on tariffs and visa bans, the Iran sanctions campaign, Syria's removal from the terrorism list, and a World Cup exit. Mexico leads on football, France leads on Dolly Parton and the Fed, and Kenya looks at the fine print of US health money.

12 countries. The Meta child-safety settlement is the day's most widely carried American story, running in Paris, Brussels and Nairobi, with each outlet asking what a US courtroom deal means for its own users. Iran sanctions and the Canada tariff fight dominate the economic pages in Doha, Ankara and Mexico City, while Seoul, Tokyo and Buenos Aires track what Washington wants from them. Away from politics there is Dolly Parton's death, a fencing federation betting on the LA Games, and a fight over whether the Kennedy Center gets torn down.

12 countries. The $40 trillion US debt figure travels furthest today, carried by Al Jazeera, Euronews and, with relish, Russian state television. The Iran sanctions push shapes coverage in Doha, Ankara and Johannesburg, while Seoul and Kyiv track what Washington is promising them and what it is quietly withholding. Away from geopolitics, outlets pick up the dropped Powell investigation, a lawsuit by Democratic states over tariffs, troops on the streets of Washington, and a promised golden age of American spaceflight.

11 countries today.
